dossier.architecture: Rebuilt compact fixed-heading shooter with rack elevator and integrated chain/trap system.

subsystems.drivetrain: Rebuild uses 26-by-27.5-inch base, deeper rails and thicker belly pan.
subsystems.intake: Protected intake with titanium rollers; dead-axle feeder preserves a short path.
subsystems.transfer: Direct shot path; reverse shooter feed and kicker transfer to amp elevator.
subsystems.scoring: Four-motor differential-speed launcher optimized for short time-to-shoot and long-range shots.
subsystems.endgame: Rack-and-pinion amp/trap elevator; individual hooks and passive stage-reaction forks.
subsystems.controls: Multiple Limelight lenses cover distant/near targets, note detection and climb alignment; one-driver controls.

versions: Original larger, maximum-weight turret robot replaced between Weeks 2 and 5. Team cited poor intake performance and inadequate long-range shot; rebuilt without turret.
dossier.analysis: A crucial counterexample to assuming the most capable-looking architecture wins: their rebuild deliberately surrendered turret freedom to improve acquisition, launch speed, weight and range.
limits: Only source-established configurations and changes are described; intermediate revisions may remain unresolved.

context_documents.title: 2024-4414 · The rebuild traded turret freedom for structure and long-range consistency
context_documents.body:
# 2024-4414: The rebuild traded turret freedom for structure and long-range consistency

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The source distinguishes the original turret from a rebuilt fixed-heading launcher. The rebuild changes drive tubes to 3×1, belly-pan thickness to 3/16 inch and base dimensions to 26×27.5 inches. Protected dead-axis feed and four-motor differential-speed shooting serve long range; reverse feeding sends a note to the amp elevator.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team reports structural problems affecting under-bumper acquisition and insufficient original turret power for its preferred long shot. It decided the turret’s advantages did not outweigh its costs for the intended robot functions.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

This is a strategic architecture rejection with concrete technical causes. A turret is not automatically superior when its packaging reduces stiffness, collection quality or release capability. The fixed-heading replacement must still pay chassis-aiming time and defended heading constraints, so the reason applies to the team’s specific route/shot strategy rather than every Crescendo robot.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Compare full acquisition-to-release time and range under defense, inspect frame deflection, and test reversed amp transfer after long shots. Preserve original/rebuild boundaries in any inspiration sentence.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/bmybbP0aJqo](https://youtu.be/bmybbP0aJqo)

source_reviews.title: HighTide announces TIDEPOD
facts: HighTide presented TIDEPOD in late March after an earlier machine.
source_reviews.limitations: Community visual guesses in replies do not establish hardware specifications.

source_reviews.title: TIDEPOD thread technical Q&A
source_reviews.locator: Posts in late-thread replies about first robot turret and double-sided belts
source_reviews.review_basis: Read technical discussion, distinguishing design contexts
facts: The thread distinguishes an earlier turret machine. A double-sided belt reply describes iterative layout and several printed idler sizes for tension after break-in.
source_reviews.limitations: No CAD measurement. Keep the earlier turret description separate from TIDEPOD.

source_reviews.title: HighTide Behind the Bumpers
facts: The rebuild is described as a fixed-heading differential shooter, reverse transfer to amp/trap elevator, separate hooks and stage-reaction forks.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: TIDEPOD is the later 2024 machine in the corpus. Its inherited layout puts a short direct speaker path ahead of the alternate placement path. In that account the team can shoot as soon as a note reaches the launch assembly and the chassis is aimed, while amp and trap use a reversal and elevator. The thread confirms that questions about the earlier turret refer to a separate design. That distinction matters when evaluating which drivetrain motions substitute for turret yaw.
piece_flow: A protected inset collector supplies the short feeder, according to the inherited study.
For speaker, the main path feeds directly through the launcher. For amp or trap the note reverses and a kicker sends it toward the raised scorer.
The inherited endgame description pairs hook engagement and passive stage reaction with placement from a rack elevator.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: A short main path keeps intermediate travel small but can leave little room to sense and stop a note before it reaches the launcher. The rack and guides occupy a second envelope, and the chain approach adds a third. Draw both floor and loaded endgame poses. In the loaded pose the forks need a usable stage reaction without forcing the elevator to take the main chassis reaction.

subsystems.name: Protected intake and feeder
subsystems.construction: Older dossier describes titanium intake rollers and a dead-axle feeder. The thread describes double-sided belt layout and replaceable printed idlers.
subsystems.operation: Gather and move the note with opposed rollers. Maintain usable belt wrap and tension as parts settle.
subsystems.team_rationale: The technical reply describes sizing several idlers so tension could be restored after break-in.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: An idler change affects tension and tooth wrap together. Repeatedly increasing its diameter can close a service or piece clearance and increase bearing load.
subsystems.interfaces: Belt routing, roller spacing and a clean path to remove the idler.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect wear and tooth engagement during both feed directions. Confirm that a usable spare idler fits without moving feed datums.
subsystems.unknowns: Belt pitch, tension window, material, measured wear.

subsystems.name: Fixed-heading shooter and alternate branch
subsystems.construction: Inherited four-motor launcher with independently set wheel speeds, plus reverse feed and kicker for placement.
subsystems.operation: Aim with chassis heading and set release angle/speed. Reverse and route the piece for amp or trap.
subsystems.team_rationale: The older study describes time-to-shoot and range as rebuild priorities.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Fast wheel readiness yields little if the robot still needs to rotate or acquire a field pose. Compare shot-ready time from the actual pickup heading and note condition.
subsystems.interfaces: Chassis aim, feed confirmation, flywheel readiness and kicker must avoid conflicting commands.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test deliberate note reversal from partial entry and inspect recovery after a failed placement handoff.
subsystems.unknowns: Wheel compression, actual shot map and readiness logic.

subsystems.name: Rack placement and climb
subsystems.construction: Older study describes rack elevator, individual hooks and passive reaction forks.
subsystems.operation: Engage chain and use the stage reaction to establish placement geometry.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Ground-relative height alone is insufficient. The placement opening moves relative to the chassis as the hooks load and forks contact the stage.
subsystems.interfaces: Hook line, fork contact and elevator travel must clear one another.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check asymmetric catch, fork misalignment and post-impact rack mesh before lifting.
subsystems.unknowns: Dimensions, loads and observed endgame rates.

revisions: TIDEPOD announcement is dated late March. Exact configurations and event cutover need primary drawings or captions.
transferable_principles: Put the common shot on a direct feed when alternative delivery is less frequent. Validate the reverse path and its recovery separately.
disconfirming_conditions: Direct-path gains erode if the pickup heading often opposes the shot heading or if a congested field requires alternate release points. A passive stage reaction only transfers to consistent legal contact geometry.
remaining_gaps: Full captions, as-built comparison with earlier machine, control source and load data.
recommended_images: TIDEPOD side view with front/rear identified
Rack and fork contact geometry in loaded endgame pose
